1380. 25. Jänner. 0. A0. — Peter und Johann, Brüder von Rosenberg, wieder holen an das Stift und Spital zu Hohenfurt die Schenkung der Dörfer Nessel bach, Einsiedl und Konradschlag, vermehren dieselbe mit dem Dorf e Lahren- becher und bestimmen die Leistungen, zu denen das Stift dem Spitale gegenüber verpflichtet sei. 1380. 14. Mai. Krumau. — Woyslaus von Dubowa verkauft dem Jendlinus von Chwalin den Wald unterhalb des Dorfes Chwalin um vier Schock Prayer Groschen.

CLVII. In nomine domini amen. Ne humani actus operum precipuo pietatis sub decursu temporis per maliciam seu qu;nncumque aliam 12* 180 bominum negligenciam a memoria euellantur, necease est, eos ma xime scripturarum testimonio frequencius renouare. Quamobrem nos Petrus et Johannes fratres de Rosemberg ad vuiuersorum noticiam volumus deuenire, quod ex salubri mentis feruore fideliter cupientes, ne nobilis domini domini Petri de Rosemberg genitoris nostri et Ka therine conthoralis sue genitricisque nostre karissime ac aliorum nostrorum predecessorum feruor deuocionis ac caritatis zelus, quem erga monastenum in Altowado fratrum sancti Benedict! ordinis Ci- ster'ciensis et precipue erga hospitale, quod prefatus genitor noster iuxta prefatum monasterium pro pauperibus nutriendis, ut inferi us patebit, in Christi et sue matris nomine erigendo de nouo suis liberis bonis f¡deliter dotauit, ac in ceteris operibus caritatis necnon in sua- rum elargicione elemosinarum deuocius in vita et in morte finaliter habuerunt, per quemcumque modum aut formam in obliuionem deducatur, sed ut ipsorum nostrorum predeeessorum omnium in anni- uersariis et singulis priuatis et generalibus deuocionibus per fratres in dicto monasterio deo famulantes necnon per pauperes in prefato bospitali decumbentes memoria in deo vigiluncior iugiter habeatur: omnia priuilegia prefati hospitalis statum dotacionem et aliam ipsius disposicionem necnon et predictorum fratrum quasdam speciales pitancias singulariter tangencia anno domini millesimo trecentesimo octuagesimo in die conuersionis sancti Pauli vidimus legimus sana non rasa nee violata sed in omni suorum parte integra invenimus, quorum priuilegorium clausulas puncta et articulos validiores et in omni parte plus necessarios ad cautelam monasterio et hospitali prefatis summe competentes huic littere non inmerito fidelissime duximus inlroponi. In quorum priuilegorium vno continebatur, quod prefatus genitor noster dominus Petrus de Rosemberg dedit et assig- nauit perpetue possidendam dicto monasterio in Altowado villam Neslboch cum aratura et pomerio eidem ville adiacente cum omni bus juribus atque agris cultis et incultis pratis pascuis aquis aqua- rninve decursibus rubetis montibus planiciebus emolimentis censibus aliisque vtilitatibus et pertinenciis vniuersis, que nunc ibi sunt auf fieri poterint in futurum, ita ut predicti fratres in prefato hospitali sex pauper es enutrire et teuere debeant per modum et formam, que inferius annotantur. Insuper in dicto priuilegio prefatus genitor noster disposuit, ut die sancti Kalixti anniuersarius suus in sepedicto claustro singulis annis solimpniiis peragatur sic videlicet, ut vigilie 181 majores ad vesperam decantentur et in crastino dominus abbas, nisi legittima causa prepeditus fuerit, missam summam debeat celebrare, reliqui vero fratres sacerdotes, quotquot fuerint, missas dicere non negligant eodem die pro anima sua ¡rc suurum omnium predecessorum et omnium fidelium defunctorum, ut tenentur. Eodem die prandium cum pitanciis in refectorio singulis laucius porrigatur ducentis quo- que pauperibus, eodem die victus pro vna uice tribuatur, vnicuique vnum denarium Wienensem tribuendn iniungentes eisdem pauperi bus, ut anime sue ¡te predecessorum suorum et omnium fîdelium defunctorum in suis orationibus memorentur. Ceterum idem genitor noster rogat et bortatur, ut omnes monachi tam clerici quam laici singulis diebus in suis specialibus deuocionibus ob respectum diuine remuneracionis sui dignentur perpetue memorari. Hoc autem facien dum perpetue sic conscienciis abbatis et priuris loci predicti eom- mittimus, quodsi aliquid de prescripts obmiserint, quatenus sciant, se penam, qua nos ratificarunt, incurrisse et rationem de hoc in die iudicii reddituros. Preterea in secunda dicti mouasterii priuilegiorum littera legendo invenimus, quod nos Petrus et Johannes prefati nec- non Jodocus et Vlricus fratres, duru adhuc indiuisi essemus, antefato monasterio seu hospitali dedimus et perpetue assignauimus vnam villam Aynsidel nominatam, quam pro centum viginti quatuor sexa- genis grossorum comparauimus cum omni vtilitate ac toto dominio ad eam pertinente adiungendo vnam libram denariorum Wyenensis monete perpetui census in theloneo nostro Rosemberg, primos dena- rios recipiendos, pro unimahus dilecte genitricis nostre domine Katherine de Rosemberg et domine Margarethe de Baworow amitte nostre felicisrecordacionis cum condicionibus infrascriptis, ita videlicet ut tercio die post festum sancti Ambrosii in anniuersario prefate geni tricis nostre vigilie maiores de vespere et in crastino misse cantate et lecte cum aliis cerimonialibus obseruationibus singulis annis per fratres tam clericos quam layos fideliter et solempniter obseruen- tur, ut in auniuersario genitoris nostri extat superius annota tum. Illo namque die fratribus ad refectorium pro prandio seu pitancia vna sexagena grossorum et pro prandio quindecim pauperum, qui ipso die nutriri debentur (sic), octo grossi annis singulis efficaciter tribuantur. Insuper secunda sexagena de redditibus prelate ville Ayn- siedel in singulis quatuor temporibus fratribus ad conuentum per YDum fertonem diuidenda pro pitanciis tribuatur, ita tamen 182 in ¡lus quatuor temporibus vno die quilibet fratrum pro anima ipsius domine genitricis nostre dicat septem psalmos penitentiales cum letania et in missis suis piam eiusdem memoriam habere tenebuntur. Idem dispositum et ordinatum est, ut tercio die post sancti Viti dies anniuersarius prefato amitte nostre domine Margarethe de Baworow in omnibus cerimoniis et aliis solempnitatibus. ut in exequiis funeralibus fundatorum prefati monasterii fieri est consuetum, per abbatem et fratres elencos et laicos in vigiliis et missis ac nratio- nibus cum summa deuocione et diligencia peragatur et fratribus ad conuentum pro prandio eodem die vna sexagena grossorum et pro prandio triginta pauperum semel nutriendornm duodecim grossi assig- nentur et ipsis triginta pauperibus post refectionem cuilibet vnus denarius Wyenensis caritatiue in domino porrigatur. Residuus vero census prefate ville Aynsidel in vtilitatem et vsum pauperum dicti hospitalis fideliter reseructur, super quo censu quatuor pauperes duo videlicet pro anima genitricis uostre et duo pro anima amitte nostre in prefato hospitali nutriendi et tenendi graciosius augeantur per modum similiter et formam , ut inferius continetur. Ceterum in tercia litlera vidimus, quod nos Petrus Vlricus el Johannes fratres prefuti de Rosember-g, dum adhuc diuisi non essemus, prefato mo nasterio et hospitali pro anima beate recordacionis domiui Jodoci de Rosemherg fratris nostri karissimi ac pro finali ipsius testamento vnam villam dictam Chunratslag cum omnium et singulorum fructuum redituum ac prouentuum vniuersa vtilitate ad eam singulariter uel generaliter spectante contulimus dctlmms et efficaciter assignauimus, prefalam villam per fratres dicti monasterii regendam et perpetue possidendam, ita tamen, quod in die anniuersario memorati fratris nostri ornnia et singula, que in ct-lebracione anniuersariorum dicti monasterii fundatorum in cultu diuino per fratres clericos et layeos et in refectione fratrum consueuerunt, singulis annis in die saucti Johannis baptiste et in crastino deuocius obseruentur, et in ipso die sexaginta pauperes cum cereuisia et pane fideliterpascantur, ipsorum cuilibet per vnum denarium Wyenensem largiendo; et super censu residuo prefate ville Chunratslag pro anima prefati fratris nostri domini Jodoci clare memorie in antedicto hospitali duo pauperes perpetuo augeantur, qui pauperes cum aliis supradictis in ipso ho spitali teneri et foueri debent, uelut postea lucidius exprimetur. Nos insuper Petrus et Johannes sepefati de Rosemberg cupientes iuxta 183 ewangeliste consilium licet inmeriti amicos nobis de iniquitatis mammona celestes efficere ac de terrena substancia per pietatis stndia quamuis modica thezauros inmarcescibiles in celestibus aggre- gare, et vt nostri in predicto loco per fratres et pauperes in vita nostra et post mortem inpressior et zelancior habeatur memoria, prefatis monasterio et hospitali villam nostram hereditariam wlga- riter Larenpecher nuncupatam cum duobus molendinis et piscina ad eam pertinentibus, que omnia simul pro ceusu et quauis alia vtilitale annuatim soluunt duodecim libras et tres solidos Wyenensium dena- riorum, cum agris cultis et incultis pratis pascuis rubetis iudicio et dominio ac qualibet alia libertate ad predictam villam in omnibus suis metis diuisim uel generaliter quocumque modo spectantibus conferimus donamus et per presentes perpetuo resignamus cum con- dicionibus hie notabiliter sub expressis, ita videlicet quod ad votum et voluntatem nostram et omnium successorum nostrorum dominorum tamen de Rosemberg abbas prefati monasterii in Altowado vnum de suis confratribus, quemcumque protunc domini de Rosemberg duxe- rint eligendum, prefato hospitali et pauperibus in proeuracione efficiat et disponat, cui idem abbas sub inveccione et districcione obediencie sanete mandet strictissime et iniungat, quatenus idem frater seu procurator predicti hospitalis omnes defectus detracciones et iniuriosas abrogaciones, si quas predictus abbas uel suus conuen tus pauperibus prefatis inferre quouis modo uel irrogare injuriose aliqualiter conarentur, ad audienciam dominorum de Rosemberg nostrorum successorum per se uel per aliam personam aut per scriptum deferre valeat atque possit, in hoc timorem et disciplinam seu rigorem abbatis et ordinis sui nichil penitus formidando, ut idem frater seu hospitalis procurator consilio dominorum pro tune de Rosemberg et auxilio mediante tales iniurias per abbatem uel suos fratres ipsis infirmis ululas per hunc modum ammouendo saltim valeat propulsare. Idem eciam procurator seu frater de diligencia et fidelitate circa predictos pauperes et bospitale per ipsum seruanda ad nostras et nostrorum successorum dominorum de Rosemberg ma- nus promissum et fídem faciat sine fraude de mandato et obediencia sui conuentus et abbatis. Denique ordiuamus et volumus, ut in pre- fato hospitali superius nominati vndecim pauperes et pro duodecimo paupere vna honesta et prouida ancilla, que ipsis pauperibus in om nibus eorum necessitatibus seruire et administrare valeat, caritatiue 184 tenoantnr et in domino foueantur perpetue in hunc modum, ita vide licet ut ipsis duodecim personis de coquina familie domini abhatis omnibus diebus omnia fercula communia, uelut ipsius domini sbbatis seruitoribus dari et minisfrari consueuerunt, sine quauis diminucione in perpetuum trihuatur, in melioracionem vero qualibet septimana, qua carnes a ceteris Christi fidelibus manducantur, triglnta duo Wyenenses denarii ipsis pauperibus cum scitu eorum procuratorio pro carnibus emendis recentibus assignentur. Et omnthus diebus ieiuniorum statutis ab ecclesia ad ieiunandum et consuetis omnibus pauporibus in communi vnam libram puri olei papaueris uel canapi tribuendo cuilibet pauperi per vnum allec singulariter uel equiualens ferculum, si alleca sine fraude nullo modo possent haberi, ipse abbas de predicta sua coquina assignai mandet fideliter et disponat. Insuper volumus et ordinamus, quod ipsis pauperibus ad braxandam specialiter ceruisiam s''\ bona ordeacea brasca de humulo, quantum ad ipsa brasea necesserfuerit, ad requisicionem suprasrripti procu- ratoris annis slngulis tiibuantur, quod et ipsa ceruisia per tamiliam et seruitores domini abbatis in suo braxatorio braxata demum ad maudatum procurators per eosdem seruitores ad celare pauperum deportetur, ac singulis annis cuilibet ¡nfirmorum pro lineis vestibus quinque vine cum dimidia in festo sancti Georgii erogentur necnon vnicuique kc!o iufirmorum infra duos annos de nouem vlnis eiusdem linei patmi pro duobus lintheamibus (sic) in festo sancti Georgii prouideatur. Et similiter infra diíífs annos cuilibet infirmorum sex vine grisei panni de lana facti pro tunica uel palio in festo sancti Wenczeslai trihuantur, cuius panni vlnam ipse abbas pro decem et septem denariis debet minime comparare. Ceterum volumus, ut sex vacce pro speciali emendacione et melioracione ipsorum pauperum in byeme per fenum et stramina, in estate vero per pastorem dicti abbatis seruando debent fideliter enutriri. Si vero predictarum vac- carum aliqua uel earum plures mortue fuerint, ad restauracionem ipsarum prefatum abbatem nolumus (?) obligare. Et quidquid in sup- plemento predietorum omnium statutorum per abbatem uel suum con- uentum neglectum uel abstractum fuerit, hoc prefatus procurator ipsius hospitalis sine omni timore sui abbatis et conuentus salua conscieucia et sui ordinis rigore ad nos seu nostros successores dominos de Rosemberg deuoluere et deferre potent, uelut extat superius lucide declaratum. Vltimo in умa Httera vidimus, quod nostri antecessores in fnndacione prefati monasterii veras decimas de suis araturis in villa Hlawatecz prope Podiehus ipsi monasterio perpetuo assignauerunt, pro quibus decimis in forma cambii et permutacionis prefato monasterio in quinque laneis in villa nostra Humpno quinque sexagenas grossorum et decem pullos anni et perpetuis census assig- nauimus et derlimu?, ipsos laneos cum omnibus suis vtilitatihus pre (sic) sepefatum monasterium perpetuo possidendos, ulla nostra nec- non nostrorum successorum instancia non obstante. In quorum omnium euidenciam et robur firmitatis sigilla nostra propria de certa sciencia nostra et pro maiori testimonio sigillum fratris nostri domini Vlrici etiam de Rosemberg presentibus duximus appendenda. Actum et datum anno die et loco quibus supra. Über die Siegel der Urkundenausstelier siehe CIV und CXIV. Beide sowie das folgende hängen an Pergamentstreifen und sind in rothes Wachs gedruckt. Roseberg. CLvm. 1380. 14. Mai. Krumau. — Woyslaus von Dubowa verkauft dem Jendlinus von Chwalin den Wald unterhalb des Dorfes Chwalin um vier Schock Prayer Groschen. Ego Woyslaus de Dubowa tenore presencium vniuersis, ad quos presentes deuenerint, rocognosco, quia non per errorem aut inpro- uide sed sana mentis fretus deliberacione siluam meam, quam habui sub uilla Chwalin proximam totam, discreto Jendlino ibidem de Chwalin meo fratueli dilecto eiusque heredibus pro quatuor sexa- genis grossorum Pragensium michi plene solutis legittime uendidi et hereditarie ad perpetuam possessionem libere resignaui, promit- tens nichilominus sincera tide vnacum discretis viris Prziedotha de Sbynycz Johanne dicto Holeska de Crasticz meis in bac parte condis- brigatoribus dictam siluam jure terre regni Boemie dudum appro- bato pre impeticione cuiusuis hominis et persone et specialiter pre dotalicio Buzcze vxoris mee post obitum meum ad triennium fideliter disbrigare. entries.english:
1380, 25 January. — Peter and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, renew for the monastery and hospital at Hohenfurt the donation of the villages Nesselbach, Einsiedl, and Konradschlag; they enlarge it with the village of Lahrenbecher and specify the obligations incumbent on the monastery toward the hospital.

CLVII. In the name of the Lord, amen. So that the works of human action, especially works of piety, may not be erased from memory over time through malice or any other negligence of men, it is necessary to renew them frequently, above all by the testimony of written records. Therefore we, Peter and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, wish it to be known to all that, earnestly desiring that the devotion and zeal of charity shown by our noble lord father, Lord Peter von Rosenberg, and his wife and our dearest mother Katherine, as well as by our other predecessors, toward the monastery at Altowado of the brothers of the Order of Cistercians of Saint Benedict—and especially toward the hospital, which our aforesaid father newly established beside the monastery in the name of Christ and his mother for the care of the poor, as will be set out below—together with their other works of charity and their generous almsgiving, may not in any way be consigned to oblivion, whether in life or at death, but that all our predecessors may continually be remembered before God at their anniversaries and at each private and general devotion by the brothers serving God in that monastery and by the poor lying in that hospital: in the year of the Lord 1380, on the day of the Conversion of Saint Paul, we saw and read all the privileges concerning the status, endowment, and other arrangements of the aforesaid hospital, as well as those touching particular provisions for the aforesaid brothers. We found them sound, unerased, unviolated, and wholly intact in every part. We have therefore rightly and faithfully deemed it appropriate to insert into this letter, for the protection of the monastery and hospital, the clauses, points, and articles of those privileges that are stronger and most necessary in every respect.

One of those privileges stated that our aforesaid father, Lord Peter von Rosenberg, gave and assigned to the monastery at Altowado, to be held in perpetuity, the village of Nesselbach, with its ploughland and the orchard adjoining the village, together with all rights, cultivated and uncultivated fields, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, thickets, hills, plains, revenues, rents, and all other benefits and appurtenances now there or that may come to be there in the future. In return, the aforesaid brothers were to feed and maintain six poor people in the hospital according to the manner and provisions set out below.

Moreover, our aforesaid father ordained in that privilege that his anniversary be solemnly observed every year in the said monastery on Saint Calixtus’s Day: the greater vigils were to be sung in the evening, and on the following day the lord abbot, unless prevented by a legitimate cause, was to celebrate high mass; all the other brothers who were priests were also to say masses that day for his soul, the souls of all his predecessors, and all the faithful departed, as they are bound to do. On that day a meal with a special dish was to be served generously to each brother in the refectory, and food for one meal was to be given to two hundred poor people, each of whom was to receive one Viennese denarius. The poor were to be enjoined to remember his soul, the souls of his predecessors, and all the faithful departed in their prayers. Furthermore, our father asks and exhorts all monks, both clerical and lay, to remember him perpetually each day in their private devotions, in hope of divine reward. We entrust the perpetual fulfilment of this to the consciences of the abbot and prior of that place; if they omit any of the foregoing, they are to know that they will incur the penalty to which they have bound themselves and will have to give account of it on the Day of Judgment.

Furthermore, on reading a second charter among the monastery’s privileges, we found that we, the aforesaid Peter and Johann, together with our brothers Jodocus and Ulrich, while we were still undivided, gave and assigned in perpetuity to the aforesaid monastery or hospital a village named Einsiedl, which we had bought for 124 score of groschen, with all its appurtenances and full lordship, adding a perpetual annual rent of one pound in Viennese coin from our toll at Rosenberg, the first payment to be collected. This was for the souls of our beloved mother, Lady Katharina von Rosenberg, and our aunt, Lady Margaret von Baworow, of happy memory, under the following conditions. Every year, on the third day after the feast of Saint Ambrose, the anniversary of our aforesaid mother was to be observed faithfully and solemnly by the brothers, both clerical and lay: the greater vigils were to be held in the evening, and masses sung and read on the following day, along with the other customary ceremonies, as set out above for our father’s anniversary. On that day, one score of groschen was to be paid each year to the brothers’ community for their meal or special dish, and eight groschen for a meal for fifteen poor people who were to be fed that day. In addition, from the revenues of the aforesaid village of Einsiedl, a second score of groschen was to be distributed to the brothers’ community at each of the four Ember seasons, one fourth at a time, for special dishes. At each of those four seasons, on one day, every brother was also to say the seven penitential psalms with the litany for the soul of our aforesaid mother and to remember her piously in his masses.

It was likewise ordained and arranged that the anniversary of our aunt, Lady Margaret von Baworow, be observed on the third day after Saint Vitus’s Day with all the ceremonies and solemnities customary at the funeral rites of the founders of the aforesaid monastery. The abbot and the brothers, clerical and lay, were to carry it out with the utmost devotion and care, with vigils, masses, and prayers. On that day one score of groschen was to be assigned to the brothers’ community for its meal, and twelve groschen for a meal for thirty poor people to be fed once; after the meal each of those thirty poor people was to be charitably given one Viennese denarius in the Lord. The remaining rent from the aforesaid village of Einsiedl was to be faithfully reserved for the use and benefit of the hospital’s poor. From that rent four poor people were to be added to those maintained in the hospital, namely two for the soul of our mother and two for the soul of our aunt, and cared for according to the manner and provisions set out below.

Furthermore, in a third charter we saw that we, Peter, Ulrich, and Johann, the aforesaid brothers von Rosenberg, while we were still undivided, gave, donated, and effectively assigned to the aforesaid monastery and hospital, for the soul of our dearest brother Jodocus von Rosenberg, of blessed memory, and in fulfilment of his final testament, a village called Konradschlag, with all the benefits pertaining to it, specifically or generally, from every kind of fruit, rent, and revenue. The village was to be administered and held in perpetuity by the brothers of that monastery, on condition that every year, on the anniversary of our aforesaid brother, all the observances customary at the anniversaries of the monastery’s founders—in divine worship by the clerical and lay brothers and in the brothers’ meal—be devoutly performed on Saint John the Baptist’s Day and the following day. On that day sixty poor people were to be faithfully fed with beer and bread, each receiving one Viennese denarius. From the remaining rent of the aforesaid village of Konradschlag, two poor people were to be added permanently to the hospital for the soul of our aforesaid brother, Lord Jodocus, of clear memory. They were to be maintained and cared for in that hospital together with the poor mentioned above, as will be explained more fully below.

Moreover, we, the aforesaid Peter and Hans von Rosenberg, wishing, in accordance with the Evangelist’s counsel, though unworthy, to make heavenly friends for ourselves from the mammon of iniquity and, through works of mercy, however modest, to store up imperishable treasures in heaven, and wishing that the brothers and poor at that place remember us more earnestly and zealously in our lifetime and after our death, hereby grant, donate, and by this present charter permanently convey to the aforesaid monastery and hospital our hereditary village commonly called Lahrenbecher, with its two mills and fishpond, all of which together yield annually twelve pounds and three shillings in Viennese denarii in rent and other benefits, together with cultivated and uncultivated fields, meadows, pastures, thickets, jurisdiction and lordship, and every other liberty belonging to that village within all its boundaries, whether separately or collectively and in whatever manner. This grant is subject to the conditions expressly stated here. At our wish and that of all our successors, the lords von Rosenberg, the abbot of the aforesaid monastery at Altowado shall appoint and assign to the hospital and its poor one of his fellow brothers, whom the lords von Rosenberg then choose, as its procurator. Under holy obedience, the abbot shall strictly command and enjoin that brother or procurator to bring before the lords von Rosenberg, our successors, in person, through another person, or in writing, any failings, derogations, or wrongful injuries which the aforesaid abbot or his convent might inflict or attempt to inflict upon those poor people. In doing this he is to fear nothing whatever of the abbot’s authority, discipline, or severity of his order, so that, with the counsel and help of the lords von Rosenberg then in office, the brother or hospital procurator may at least be able to remove in this way such injuries inflicted by the abbot or his brothers upon those sick people. The procurator or brother shall also give us and our successors, the lords von Rosenberg, his pledge and promise, without deceit, that he will diligently and faithfully care for those poor people and the hospital, under the command and obedience of his convent and abbot.

Finally, we ordain and wish that the eleven poor people named above, and, as a twelfth person, one respectable and prudent servant woman able to serve and attend to all their needs, be charitably maintained and cared for in the Lord in that hospital forever, as follows. Every day, all twelve are to be given from the abbot’s household kitchen all the common dishes customarily served to the abbot’s own servants, without any reduction. In addition, each week when other Christians eat meat, thirty-two Viennese denarii are to be assigned to the poor, with the knowledge of their procurator, for the purchase of fresh meat. On all fast days prescribed by the Church and custom, the abbot is faithfully to arrange from his kitchen for all the poor together to receive one pound of pure poppy or hemp oil, and each poor person is to receive one herring or an equivalent dish, if herrings cannot in any way be obtained without fraud. Furthermore, we ordain that every year, at the request of the aforesaid procurator, good barley malt and as much hops as are needed for the brew be supplied specifically for brewing beer for the poor. The abbot’s household and servants shall brew that beer in his brewery and then, at the procurator’s order, carry it to the poor people’s chamber. Each year, on Saint George’s Day, five and a half ells of linen are to be given to each of the sick for linen garments. Within two years, each sick person is also to be provided on Saint George’s Day with nine ells of the same coarse linen for two bedsheets. Similarly, within two years, each sick person is to receive six ells of grey woollen cloth for a tunic or mantle on Saint Wenceslas’s Day; the abbot is to buy each ell of this cloth for no more than seventeen denarii. We also wish six cows to be faithfully kept for the special improvement and better provision of the poor, fed on hay and straw in winter and tended in summer by the abbot’s shepherd. If any of those cows, or several of them, die, we do not wish the aforesaid abbot to be bound to replace them. Whatever in the fulfilment of all the foregoing provisions is neglected or withheld by the abbot or his convent, the hospital procurator may, without fear of his abbot and convent and with a clear conscience and due regard to his order, report to us or our successors, the lords von Rosenberg, as was clearly stated above.

Lastly, in another charter we saw that our predecessors, at the foundation of the aforesaid monastery, assigned to it in perpetuity the true tithes from their ploughlands in the village of Hlawatecz near Podiehus. In exchange for those tithes, we assigned and gave to the monastery, by way of exchange, five holdings in our village of Humpno, five score of groschen, ten chickens annually, and perpetual rents, granting the monastery permanent possession of those holdings with all their appurtenances, notwithstanding any claim by us or our successors. As evidence and confirmation of all this, we have, of our certain knowledge, caused our own seals and, for greater testimony, the seal of our brother Lord Ulrich von Rosenberg to be attached to this charter. Done and given in the year, day, and place stated above.

The seals of the issuers are described under numbers CIV and CXIV. Both seals, as well as the following one, hang from parchment strips and are impressed in red wax. Ulrich’s seal shows a Gothic niche containing a shield with a five-petalled rose; a rose of the same kind also ornaments the helmet above the shield. Inscription: “Seal of Ulrich von Roseberg.”

CLVIII. 1380, 14 May. Krumau. — Woyslaus von Dubowa sells to Jendlinus von Chwalin the forest below the village of Chwalin for four score of Prague groschen.

I, Woyslaus von Dubowa, by this present instrument acknowledge to all to whom it may come that, not in error or rashly but with sound judgment, I have lawfully sold to the prudent Jendlinus of Chwalin, my dear kinsman, and to his heirs, for four score of Prague groschen fully paid to me, my entire forest lying below the village of Chwalin, and have freely conveyed it to him hereditarily for perpetual possession. I further promise in good faith, together with the prudent men Prziedotha of Sbynycz and Johann called Holeska of Crasticz, my fellow guarantors in this matter, to defend the aforesaid forest, according to the law of the land of the Kingdom of Bohemia long established, against the claim of any person, and especially against any claim arising from the dower of my wife Buzcze, for three years after my death. We, Prziedotha of Sbinicz and Johann of Crasticz, the aforesaid guarantors of the forest, likewise declare that we are its guarantors and promise to defend it against every claim as stated above. If, God forbid, one of us guarantors should die before the three-year period of warranty has expired, we shall appoint and install an equally suitable replacement in place of the deceased within one month of his death. We renew this present instrument under penalty of three score groschen, payable to Jendlinus or his heirs within four weeks, and under the obligation of appearing as hostages at Krumau with one servant and two horses, according to the ancient custom.

Thus every four weeks we promise to pay Jendlinus or his heirs three score groschen under the aforesaid penalties and hostage obligations, until we appoint an equally suitable guarantor in place of the deceased, renewing this instrument with the force stated above. If, however, we are unable to defend the aforesaid forest as promised, we shall then convey and surrender to Jendlinus or his heirs, from our freely held hereditary lands, property of such value, increased by one third, or promise to pay them six score groschen in ready money for it. Otherwise, if we fail to convey and surrender such property to Jendlinus or his heirs, or fail to pay the six score groschen, one of us guarantors, upon being warned, shall, one month after the warning, appear as a hostage in the city of Krumau at the house of the host assigned to him, with one servant and two horses, as is customary. He shall remain there until the six score groschen due for failure to warrant the aforesaid forest, together with the damages thereby incurred and established without oath, have been paid in full.

In testimony and for the enduring validity of this matter, our seals, together with the seal of the aforesaid Woyslaus, are attached to this instrument. In the year of the Lord 1380, on Wednesday, Saint Boniface’s Day, at Krumau. Three seals in white wax hang from parchment strips. (a) A helmet with the bust of a man wielding a sword; inscription: “Seal of Woyslaus von Dubowa.” (b) A helmet with a half-moon; inscription: “Seal of Prziedota of Zbinicz.” (c) A helmet with two crossed horns; inscription: “Seal of Johann of Crasticz.” The editor notes that no feast of this name falls on a Wednesday in that year; 14 May was a Monday.
